topic.title: Getting temperature data
topic.para: This section describes two ways to read the temperature. If neither shows a temperature, the operating system has no access to a temperature sensor, as is the case in a virtual machine that does not emulate one.

section.title: Reading the ACPI thermal zones
section.para: The kernel exposes each ACPI thermal zone as a directory named /sys/class/thermal/thermal_zoneN. Reading these files requires neither the sensors package nor special privileges.

example.title: Listing the type and temperature of all ACPI thermal zones

section.para: The grep . command prints the name of each file in front of its content, so that every value stays assigned to its zone. The temperature is given in millidegrees Celsius: 40900 means 40.9°C. The type acpitz identifies an ACPI thermal zone.
If /sys/class/thermal contains no thermal_zoneN directory, the system has no ACPI thermal zone. Use the sensors command instead.
Each zone can define trip points. To list the first trip point of the first zone, run:

example.title: Listing the first trip point of an ACPI thermal zone

section.para: A trip point of type critical gives the temperature at which the kernel shuts down the system to protect the hardware. Its value is also in millidegrees Celsius: 100000 means 100°C. When a zone reaches this temperature, the kernel logs the messages critical temperature reached and HARDWARE PROTECTION shutdown (Temperature too high).

section.title: Finding out which readings come through ACPI
section.para: You can recognize a reading that comes through ACPI in two ways:

listitem.para: Its zone in /sys/class/thermal has the type acpitz.
In the output of the sensors command, its chip name is acpitz-acpi-0 and its adapter is ACPI interface.

section.para: To see the name that the system firmware gave to each zone, read the path file of the zone:

example.title: Listing the firmware names of all ACPI thermal zones

section.para: The kernel reports that a reading comes through ACPI, but not which component the zone measures. The firmware chooses the names.
Sensors that sensors lists under another chip name, such as the NVMe drive nvme-pci-0090 in the following section, are provided by their own kernel drivers and do not come through ACPI.

section.title: Reading all sensors with the sensors command
section.para: The sensors command lists every temperature sensor that the kernel has registered, not only the ACPI thermal zones. It needs the sensors package, as described in , but no special privileges. To obtain a snapshot of the current temperatures, run:
section.screen:
nvme-pci-0090 Adapter: PCI adapter Composite: +49.9°C (low = -273.1°C, high = +69.8°C) (crit = +99.8°C)
acpitz-acpi-0 Adapter: ACPI interface temp1: +40.9°C temp2: +52.9°C

callout.para: The device that reports the values. The name consists of the driver (nvme), the bus (pci) and the address of the device on that bus.
The interface through which the device is accessed, for example, PCI adapter or ACPI interface.
The temperature of the device, followed by the low, high and critical limits that the device reports.
The ACPI thermal zones. Each zone is one temperature. In this example, temp1 is thermal_zone0 (40.9°C) and temp2 is thermal_zone1 (52.9°C).

section.para: The sensors command lists the sensors that the kernel has already registered. It does not depend on sensors-detect, which only searches for additional chips (see ). The kernel drivers coretemp for Intel processors and k10temp for AMD processors provide the CPU temperature.

note.title: Output depends on the type of hardware
note.para: The output of the sensors command depends on the type of hardware installed on your machine, as different hardware components have different sensors.
